subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — NovaMed Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novamed.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@novamed.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discussion — NovaMed Health

Hi Samantha / Daniel,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have alignment. Please tell me if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Intermittent latency spikes during morning and late-afternoon traffic peaks (token-level tail latency > 700ms) impacting clinical intake workflows.
- Need for strict data isolation and customer-managed keys for PHI-sensitive prompts.
- Procurement/compliance timeline requires SOC 2 evidence and an SLA for availability.

Goals we heard:
- Stable, predictable inference performance for batch and interactive workloads (avg token latency target: ~120-180ms; 95th < 300ms).
- Dedicated GPU pool to avoid multi-tenant interference and meet isolation requirements.
- Clear scaling plan to handle scheduled load (end-of-day batch + peak interactive periods).

Proposed Dedicated capacity summary:
- Baseline: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for NovaMed (single-tenant).
- Burst policy: allow up to 16 GPUs for short windows using reserved burst credits.
- Autoscaling: policy-based scaling with warm pools to keep cold-start latency minimal (pre-warming on predictable schedules).
- Isolation: VPC-private deployment with customer KMS integration (HSM options available).
- SLAs: target 99.95% uptime for the dedicated fleet; detailed SLOs in attached SLA doc.

Attachments I attached: Novamed_Dedicated_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft), capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx (baseline & burst calc), redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will circulate SOW + capacity estimate (attached) for your review — action: Marissa (today).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra & security team next week (30-45m) — action: schedule by Friday.
3) Share SOC 2 + compliance evidence and KMS integration guide — action: Marissa (tomorrow).
4) Procurement timeline / PO target: Samantha to confirm by end of May if possible.

Can you confirm procurement timing and who from your infra/security team should join the deep-dive?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. That matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement: tentative approval process is on track; finance is targeting a decision by 05/28 but security has a SOC 2 review that may add a week. I should know by 05/24 with a firmer timeline.
- SLA: 99.95% sounds reasonable; can you confirm remedies and credits for downtime in the SOW?
- Capacity: the baseline of 8 GPUs looks right for our current traffic. During a typical peak day we see 2-3x the baseline for ~45 minutes — burst to 16 should cover that. Can you clarify warm-pool sizing?

Tech deep-dive — please include your SE (for kernel & quantization questions) and bring a brief slide of expected latency distribution under the proposed config. Our infra lead (CC'd) will join if available; I'll confirm by EOD Friday.

Thanks — Samantha

Quick technical notes from my side (SE):

- GPU type: recommend A100-80GB or equivalent (we can also size for H100 if you prefer higher throughput for dense models).
- Warm pool sizing: suggest maintaining 2 standby instances (~20% of baseline) during known peak windows; this keeps cold-start token latencies under 100ms. For your pattern (45-minute spikes) we can rely primarily on burst credits + warm pre-warming 15 minutes prior to expected peak.
- Isolation: VPC + private subnets with customer KMS for key rotation; we can support Bring-Your-Own-Key via AWS KMS / GCP KMS integrations or HSM for on-prem customers.
- Monitoring & observability: we'll enable token-level latency traces and per-route dashboards. We can set alerting thresholds and a per-route autoscaler that considers latency and queue depth.

I'll attach a quick capacity calc (capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx) showing baseline vs peak. For the deep-dive I can demo a small perf run (20-30 mins) with a representative prompt set if they want to see end-to-end latency.

Fwd-ing to schedule: Marissa, what windows next week look best to invite infra/security? I can do Tue/Wed morning.
